slide_003.text: On this slide, the focus is PRETREATMENT. The important point is to understand exactly what the slide requires and how that requirement affects inspection and coating work. The slide identifies the following key points. Pretreatment is the preparation carried out on a surface before applying paint or coating so that the coating can adhere properly and provide the required protection. In coating work, pretreatment usually includes: Cleaning – removes oil, grease, dirt, salts and other contaminants. Rust / scale removal – removes corrosion products, mill scale or old coating where required. Surface roughening / profiling – creates a suitable surface profile for coating adhesion. Chemical treatment – may include processes such as phosphating, conversion coating or other specified treatments. Final inspection – confirms the surface is clean, dry and suitable before coating application.
